findings.title: A no-op commit is reported as a successful routed fix
findings.description: `commitPathsIfChanged` returns `null` when Git reports no changes for the requested paths, including when a target is ignored. This code treats that result as success: the fix log and `fixed` count are retained, with no commit, deferral, or error. The non-invoking checkout can therefore be left with an uncommitted fix even though routed fixes are supposed to be committed there. Handle the `null` result explicitly rather than reporting the fix as successfully committed.

findings.title: Git probe failures are mislabeled as checkout state
findings.description: Both catches convert every `gitExec` rejection into a specific readiness result: `NOT_A_CHECKOUT` or `DETACHED_HEAD`. But these calls also have a timeout, and can fail for reasons such as a timeout or a missing Git executable. Those failures are silently reported as ordinary deferrals with the wrong reason, obscuring the underlying problem. Distinguish the expected Git exit status from other failures and propagate unexpected errors.
